Let’s talk about Chapter 10: The Ongoing Journey.
You know, the story of worker cooperatives in the United States isn’t finished—not by a long shot. Every new cooperative, every fresh idea, adds another chapter to a living tradition—one that’s full of struggle, change, and, most of all, hope.
To really understand this journey, let’s listen to the people who’ve lived it firsthand.
There’s the former factory worker, now an owner in her cooperative. She can still recall those early days—the fear, the uncertainty, and all those marathon meetings filled with heated debates and real moments of doubt. But looking back, what stands out even more is the pride she felt watching her business succeed. The friendships she built, the sense of purpose she found—those are the memories that matter most. Working for something bigger than herself changed everything.
Then, there’s the young organizer. He’s inspired by the stories of those who came before him, and he knows firsthand how tough it is to build alliances that cross race, class, even geography. The work? It’s challenging. The victories? Sometimes, they’re small. But to him, every cooperative—no matter its size—is one more step toward a fairer, more democratic economy.
The author leaves us with a sense that there’s still so much to do. The future isn’t set in stone, and nobody can promise what comes next. But if there’s one lesson from the past, it’s this: real change happens when everyday people come together, share their dreams, and just refuse to give up.
So, the journey carries on. Every new generation shapes it with their choices, their commitments, and their hope. And here’s the invitation—it’s open to you, too. Join the work. Learn from those who’ve come before. And let yourself imagine: what could happen if we truly dared to cooperate?
